prompt: Why does the planner count installations over the last 28 days rather than every install ever?

choices.text: The stores delete older records after a month
choices.why: The window is the planner's choice.

choices.text: Older versions send no version number
choices.why: The app sends its version with every request.

choices.text: So it counts people who use the app
choices.why: Right. Every install ever counts phones in drawers too.

choices.text: A longer window would be slower to query
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: In the lesson's table, how many of the 6081 installations would a minimum of 1.5.1 send to the update screen?
A phone is stuck on 1.2.0 because its OS cannot install 1.3. What happens if the minimum version becomes 1.3.1?

choices.text: Its owner meets a screen with no way out
choices.why: Right. An update they cannot install.

choices.text: The phone updates its OS first
choices.why: An app cannot make that happen.

choices.text: The store installs 1.3.1 anyway
choices.why: The store cannot install what the OS cannot run.

choices.text: Nothing, as 1.2.0 never reads the minimum
choices.why: The lesson assumes the check shipped early; then it does.

prompt: Match each server change to what the installed 1.3.1 does.

pairs.right: meets a value it cannot draw

prompt: Why is a new value in an existing field, like a status "skipped", not a safe addition?

choices.text: JSON does not allow new values in a string field
choices.why: JSON has no opinion on values.

choices.text: Only numbers are safe to add
choices.why: Any field can be added; values are another matter.

choices.text: It makes the response too large
choices.why: Size is not the issue.

choices.text: Old code already decided what each one means
choices.why: Right. The new one falls outside those decisions.

prompt: Which habits make an app a tolerant reader? Choose every one.

choices.text: Ignore fields it does not know
choices.why: Right. Otherwise every addition breaks it.

choices.text: Default a field that is missing
choices.why: Right. The screen still draws.

choices.text: Draw an unknown status as something neutral
choices.why: Right. An else, a fallback case, a default.

choices.text: Refuse a response with extra fields
choices.why: That is the strict parser the lesson warns about.

prompt: Put the steps of expand-then-contract in order, for replacing minutes with seconds.
items: release an app that reads seconds
wait until every version in the window reads it

prompt: In the lesson's contract.ts, why does adding seconds to the response not fail the test?

choices.text: Because seconds is a number
choices.why: Its type is never checked.

choices.text: No contract lists it, so it is never checked
choices.why: Right. That is what lets the server add fields.

choices.text: The test skips the first session
choices.why: Every session is checked.

choices.text: 1.5.2 already reads seconds
choices.why: Neither contract mentions it.

prompt: Against api-rename.ts, how many broken promises did the test list for 1.3.1?
The server keeps minutes as a number but starts rounding it differently. What does the lesson's contract test report?

choices.text: BROKEN for 1.3.1 only
choices.why: Nothing it checks has changed.

choices.text: ok for every version
choices.why: Right. It records shape; meaning needs values and a person.

choices.text: A type error for minutes
choices.why: The type is still a number.

choices.text: BROKEN for 1.3.1 and 1.5.2 alike
choices.why: Both contracts still pass.

prompt: When a version leaves the support window, delete its contract file in the same pull ___ that stops supporting it.
Put the steps of retiring an endpoint in order.
items: decide the date from the count
answer 410 with the version to install

prompt: After the sunset date, why answer 410 with a body rather than 404?

choices.text: 404 is reserved for the stores
choices.why: No such reservation.

choices.text: 410 makes the app update itself
choices.why: Nothing makes an app update itself.

choices.text: Browsers and phones cache a 404 for far too long
choices.why: The planner is not a browser.

choices.text: An old app that checks it shows what to install
choices.why: Right. A sentence instead of a blank list.

prompt: Which two parts of the contract can never be removed?

choices.text: The minimum-version check and handling 410
choices.why: Right. They are how every other part is retired.

choices.text: The sessions list and its status field
choices.why: Those can be retired, by the other two.

choices.text: The Sunset header and the Link header
choices.why: Useful warnings, but an old app may not read them.

choices.text: The /v1 and /v2 prefixes
choices.why: Versioned paths are retired too.

prompt: What does raising the app's minimum OS do to copies already installed on older phones?

choices.text: The store removes them
choices.why: Neither store does that.

choices.text: They stop opening on the next launch
choices.why: Nothing stops an installed copy from opening.

choices.text: Nothing; they keep calling your API
choices.why: Right. Only new installs and updates stop.

choices.text: They update to the last version their OS allows
choices.why: Not by themselves; they stay as they are.

prompt: A teammate proposes renaming minutes to durationMinutes in one release, since the new app reads the new name. What is the safe plan?

choices.text: Send both names until no version reads the old
choices.why: Right. Expand, then contract.

choices.text: Rename it and raise the minimum the same day
choices.why: One in five people meets an update screen that morning.

choices.text: Rename it; tolerant readers default the field
choices.why: A default is not the week's real total.

choices.text: Keep minutes forever and add nothing
choices.why: The change is possible; it just takes months.
